label: locating an event in time: it is on Monday, it is at three
note: CLOSED BY CHAPTER 102, AND THE OLD NOTE WAS HALF WRONG. It read "requires the locative on a time word, which is not taught. The parts are all present -- days, hours, the -il suffix -- and are never assembled." The parts half was accurate and the CASE was not: Malayalam fixes a clock time with the DATIVE, not the locative -- raNTu maNikku, not a form in -il -- and the dative has been taught since ML-C06-dative-ikku at sequence 320, in the same chapter that gives the reader enikku. The point was never waiting on a suffix; it was waiting on the joint. Chapter 102 supplies exactly that joint and introduces no new word at all: -kku on the hour (ML-C102-manikku), NOTHING on the named day (ML-C102-azhcha -- thiNkaLaazhcha stands in the when-slot bare, as innu and naaLe have since chapter 94), and ethra maNikku for the question (ML-C102-ethra-manikku), built on the same ethra that ML-C34-codikkuka (760) ALREADY drills as ethra maNi?, 'what hour?' -- so the question half of this point was one ENDING short, not one phrase short, and the lesson now says so. ONE LIMIT, RECORDED: the label's English is copular ('it IS on Monday, it IS at three') and the chapter produces no copular sentence. It locates an event with a fronted adjunct -- thiNkaLaazhcha raNTu maNikku nyaan pOkuM -- which is the ordinary Malayalam way; 'it is at two' would need -aaNu on the time phrase and is not taught here. Both halves of the FUNCTION are delivered, on a named day and at a named hour; the copular framing is not.
